_meta.model: ONE master index for the whole Manage Scripts tree. Flat scripts[] array. Rows: name, folder, state, body, calls, scriptRef. The renderer builds the folder tree from each row's `folder` and the CALLS/CALLED-BY graph from `calls[]`; `calledBy` is DERIVED at render time by inverting every row's calls[] and is NEVER stored. Listing is not loading: the tree + graph read only this file; a body is fetched lazily on drill-in.

bodyValues.present: The .fmscript file EXISTS at scriptRef and contains real content. Safe to drill in.
bodyValues.pending: NO FILE EXISTS at scriptRef yet. The row is a tree placeholder. Do NOT link to it as if it were readable.

_meta.bodyNote: ⚠️ `body` added 2026-07-29 AFTER A REAL FAILURE, and the failure is the reason the field exists. schemaVersion 2.1 shipped this manifest with 20 rows carrying scriptRef paths, and exactly ONE of those files existed (utilities/commitRecord.fmscript, which predated the commit). The manifest asserted a tree of readable bodies over an almost-empty directory. It is the same defect the README had one commit earlier - a document claiming to mirror something it does not - which makes it the second instance in one PR. A renderer reading 2.1 would have built a full navigable tree where 19 of 20 drill-ins 404. **A pointer is a claim. Never write one for a file you have not created.** Michael, on finding it: 'i'm very confused why scripts doesn't have a per file rendition of each script in the app... not much here is helpful rn.' He was right.
_meta.folderTreeNote: CORRECTED 2026-07-29. schemaVersion 2.0 used imports/navigation/triggers/utilities, which matched nothing in the file; README.md carries the struck claim. `utilities` survives as ONE flagged divergence holding the shared commitRecord helper - Michael to confirm whether the live file has that folder.
_meta.bodyNature: DICTATION reference (the exact steps to type into Manage Scripts, narrative as native # comment lines) - NOT paste-round-trippable, because FileMaker's script clipboard is XML. Unlike .fmcalc.
_meta.sourceOfBodies: Bodies are ported from the ClickUp per-script pages, which held real contracts, step text and in two cases full FMXML. That content was NOT invented here and NOT summarized - it was moved, with defects found during the port flagged inline rather than silently patched.
_meta.keying: Script names are unique per FileMaker file, so `name` is a safe graph key.
_meta.callsResolution: calls[] may target a script OR a custom function; the linter resolves against this file first, then functions/_index.json.

stateValues.built: Verified present in the FileMaker file on a named date.
stateValues.superseded: DO NOT IMPLEMENT. Written against an older schema. See supersededWhy.

_meta.stateNote: `state` describes the SCRIPT's standing in the FileMaker file. `body` describes whether DOCUMENTATION exists here. They are independent: a superseded script can have a full body (worth reading, do not build), and a golden script can have no body yet.
_meta.capDiscipline: Keep rows minimal so this master index stays under the ~30KB read cap. If it crosses, shard by top-level folder behind a pointer - still no renderer change.
_meta.buildOrderNote: ORDER IS A CORRECTNESS MATTER. On FMP19 there are no native transactions, so atomicity needs every write to flow through ONE relationship from ONE parent record. That parent is the ReceivedFunds receipt. Build the txn_* wrapper before the receipt table exists and the only available parent is Loans - so one check across two loans has TWO parents and Revert Record can only roll back half, shipping a silent partial rollback. Table before wrapper.
_meta.coverage: 7 of 20 bodies present (2026-07-29). Present: txn_Begin, txn_Commit, txn_Rollback, 10_UI__Set_Hub_Tab, 30_CONTEXT__Select_Property_Context, 70_SCHEDULE__Generate_Expected_Schedule, 60_PAYMENTS__Auto_Apply_Waterfall, commitRecord (8 counting the pre-existing helper). Pending bodies still have real content sitting on their ClickUp pages - porting them is mechanical, not a design task.

scripts.name: txn_Begin
scripts.note: Isolates ONE parent record as the write anchor and refuses to nest. NO engine transaction underneath - the body says so three times because the name lies.

scripts.name: txn_Commit
scripts.note: The ONLY legal Commit Records between Begin and here. Fails loudly and leaves the record uncommitted so the caller owns the rollback.

scripts.name: txn_Rollback
scripts.note: Revert Record on the PARENT discards the whole uncommitted set. Deliberately has NO repair path - prevention only.

scripts.name: 30_CONTEXT__Select_Property_Context
scripts.note: Exists to never silently pick the wrong loan. On several open loans it returns resolution:'ambiguous' with the loan global left EMPTY - an empty global is honest, a wrong one is a payment on the wrong note.

scripts.name: 10_UI__Set_Hub_Tab
scripts.note: Thin by law: NO data mutation. Validates the tab name because a typo would otherwise leave a blank panel with no error.

scripts.name: 70_SCHEDULE__Generate_Expected_Schedule
scripts.note: Idempotent via a stable ScheduleKey (fkLoan.fkStandardTransaction.SequenceNumber). ⚠️ TWO OPEN DEFECTS found during the port: Date() month-overflow breaks due dates for loans originated on the 29th-31st, and fkStatus is still a placeholder awaiting the status resolver.

scripts.name: 50_RECEIPTS__Create_ReceivedFunds_From_Document
scripts.supersededWhy: Mixes the receipt event with ledger posting; property-centered. REWRITE AGAINST ReceivedFunds (Q8 approved 2026-07-29). The irony: this script's own name proves the table was always intended.

scripts.name: 60_PAYMENTS__Post_ReceivedFunds_Batch
scripts.supersededWhy: Allocates across properties instead of loans. Its own doc says it 'does not skip the parent receipt layer' - the sentence that exposed the 9-vs-10 table gap.

scripts.name: 60_PAYMENTS__Auto_Apply_Waterfall
scripts.supersededWhy: Keys off fkProperty AND commits TWICE PER APPLIED ROW inside its loop. The commits are the worse defect: each one ends the transaction and makes prior rows permanent, so a failure mid-loop leaves the money half-applied while the routine reports success. Full body present - read it, do not build it.

scripts.name: 80_PAYOFF__Create_Payoff_From_Prior_Version
scripts.supersededWhy: Treats payoff as DOCUMENTS + versions rather than the real Payoffs table under Loans. The snapshot freeze is the second all-or-nothing routine: a partial freeze is a quote that silently changes after it was sent.

scripts.name: 80_PAYOFF__Save_Issued_Payoff_To_Binder
scripts.supersededWhy: Same payoff-as-document assumption; rewrite together with Create_Payoff_From_Prior_Version.

scripts.name: 40_BINDER__New_Document_From_Capture

scripts.name: 20_NAV__Open_Related_Loan_From_Property

scripts.name: 70_SCHEDULE__Assess_Late_Fees
